faqs.question: How much is a crop loan per acre?
faqs.answer: DBT will be given at the rate of Rs 4,000 per acre per season for cropping while zero-interest loan will be at the rate of Rs 50,000 per hectare to be capped at Rs 1 lakh per farmer, sources told BusinessToday.In. The crop loan is already offered to farmers at a subsidized rate of 4 percent only.

faqs.question: What is the lock in period for bank loans?
faqs.answer: A beneficiary cannot close the bank loans within three years from the date of availing loans.

faqs.question: What is the subsidy pattern?
faqs.answer: The subsidy is 36% of the Total Financial Outlay (TFO) for General Category candidates and 44% for Women, SC/ST/NE and Hilly State Candidates.

faqs.question: Is there any other condition for eligibility?
faqs.answer: Yes, retired employees getting pensionary benefits are not eligible for subsidy. However, they can undergo training and establish self financed projects.

faqs.question: Is there any upper ceiling for the project cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, the upper ceiling for the project cost eligible for subsidy is Rs. 20 Lakhs for individual projects and Rs. 100 Lakh for group projects. For extremely successful individual projects the ceiling is Rs. 25 Lakh.

faqs.question: Can the candidates undertake group projects?
faqs.answer: Yes, the candidates are allowed to undertake group projects, if the group consists of a total of five or more persons trained under the scheme.

faqs.question: What will happen if the project is not completed?
faqs.answer: If the project is not completed within the stipulated period, benefit of subsidy shall not be available and advance subsidy placed with the participating bank, if any, will have to be refunded forthwith to NABARD.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the training?
faqs.answer: 45 days of residential training for the students who are desirous of setting up agri-clinics and agri-business centers.

faqs.question: What is the age requirement for registration as a beneficiary under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of Odisha?
faqs.answer: The building worker must be at least 18 years old and not older than 60 years old.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum service requirement to register as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Yes, the building worker must have completed 90 days of service as a building worker in the preceding 12 months.

faqs.question: Who can apply for the welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: Any registered worker of the Board can apply for the welfare scheme.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for registering a worker as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: The District Labour Officers (D.L.O)/ Asst. Labour Officers/ Rural Labour Inspectors are acting as Registering Officers for the registration of beneficiaries under the Board.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for registration as a beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Every building worker who is between the age of 18-60 years and who has been engaged in any building or other construction work for not less than 90 days during the preceding one year is eligible for registration as a beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board of Odisha.

faqs.question: Can Odia migrant workmen be registered as beneficiaries under the Odisha Building & Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Yes, Odia migrant workmen engaged in building and other construction works in other states can be registered as beneficiaries under the Odisha Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for applying for the registration?
faqs.answer: To register as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board, an applicant worker should download Form-XXVII and attach all the mandatory documents (self attested, if required) and a fee of [?]20/- to the District Labour Officers (D.L.O)/ Asst. Labour Officers/ Rural Labour Inspectors of your area. | Alternatively, registration can also be done through the official website of the Odisha BOCWW Board: https://nirmanshramik.odisha.gov.in/obocwwb/public/cwLogin .

faqs.question: Is there a specific form for the registration through offline mode as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Yes, the application for registration must be made in Form-XXVII. You can obtain this form from the District Labour Officers (D.L.O)/ Asst. Labour Officers/ Rural Labour Inspectors in your area.

faqs.question: How much is the fee associated with the registration process?
faqs.answer: The registration fee is [?]20/- which is payable during the registration.

faqs.question: What happens after I pay the application fee?
faqs.answer: After you pay the application fee of [?]20/-, your application will be reviewed by the registering officer. The decision to approve or reject your application will be based on the merits of your application.

faqs.question: Who decides whether my application will be approved or rejected?
faqs.answer: The registering officer is responsible for deciding whether your application will be approved or rejected based on its merits.

faqs.question: Can my application be rejected even if I have paid the application fee?
faqs.answer: Yes, your application can be rejected even if you have paid the application fee. The final decision is made by the registering officer based on the merits of your application.

faqs.question: How much is the fee associated with the renewal of the registration?
faqs.answer: The renewal fee is [?]50/- which is payable during the renewal process of the registration.

faqs.question: What criteria must an applicant meet to be considered for this benefit?
faqs.answer: A nominee of a registered member is eligible for this benefit in the event of an accident causing the member to suffer a permanent total disability, loss of one limb or eye, or permanent disability without losing two limbs or eyes.

faqs.question: What kind of assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Under this scheme, the Board shall provide [?]1,50,000/- for Permanent total disability; [?]80,000/- for Loss of one limb/ eye; [?]40,000/- for Permanent disability without loss of two limbs/ eyes in the event of an accident in all cases.

faqs.question: What form needs to be used to apply for this welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: The application must be made in the prescribed Form-XXXIV. The form can be downloaded from https://bocboard.labdirodisha.gov.in/Building/homecontent/BeneficiaryForms/ACCIDENT%20Form.pdf or can be collected from the District Labour Officers (D.L.O)/ Asst. Labour Officers/ Rural Labour Inspectors of your area.

faqs.question: Where do I submit the application for this welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: Application can be submitted online on: https://nirmanshramik.odisha.gov.in/obocwwb/public/cwLogin . Alternatively , the offline application for this welfare scheme should be submitted to the District Labour Officers (D.L.O)/ Asst. Labour Officers/ Rural Labour Inspectors in your area.

faqs.question: What happens if the application is rejected?
faqs.answer: In case of rejection, the applicants would be intimated about such rejection, with due intimation to the Board.

faqs.question: What are the consequences of submitting fraudulent documents for assistance?
faqs.answer: In case of receipt of assistance on the basis of fraudulent documents, the amount released towards any assistance would be recovered from the applicant under the provisions of the OPDR Act, and his/her membership would be ceased.

tags: Homestay; Breakfast; Tourism; Accommodation
brief_description: The Directorate of Tourism, Andaman & Nicobar Administration is implementing ‘Andaman & Nicobar Bed & Breakfast/Homestay Scheme’ all over the Island based on the approved guidelines of the Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India under the scheme “Incredible India Bed & Breakfast/Homestay Establishment”.
detailed_description: The Directorate of Tourism, Andaman & Nicobar Administration, is implementing the ‘Andaman & Nicobar Bed & Breakfast/Homestay Scheme’ all over the Island based on the approved guidelines of the Ministry of Tourism, Govt. of India, under the scheme “Incredible India Bed & Breakfast/Homestay Establishment”. The concept of the scheme is to provide supplementary and quality accommodation for foreigners and domestic tourists to stay with an Indian family to experience Indian customs and traditions. | The aim of providing comfortable Home Stay Facilities of Standardized World Class Services to tourists, and to supplement the availability of accommodation in tourist destinations, the Department of Tourism, A & N Administration will classify fully operational rooms of Bed & Breakfast/ Home Stay Facilities as “Andaman & Nicobar Bed & Breakfast/ Homestay Establishments”. The basic idea is to provide a clean and affordable place for foreigners and domestic tourists alike including an opportunity for foreign tourists to stay with an Indian family to experience Indian customs and traditions and relish authentic Indian cuisine.
benefits: - The scheme will be on a bed-and-breakfast basis, and charges will have to be levied accordingly. The type of breakfast to be offered will have to be specified, the charges will have to be displayed, and the visitors will have to be informed in advance to avoid unnecessary disputes. | - Once an establishment applies for classification or reclassification, it will have to be ready at all times for inspection by the Classification Committee. No requests for deferment of inspection will be entertained. | - Classification will be valid for three years from the date of issue of orders or, in the case of reclassification, from the date of expiry of the last classification, provided that the application has been received within the stipulated time, i.e., 3 months before the expiry of the last classification. | - The application fee payable for classification or reclassification of a B&B or homestay will be as follows, and the demand draft will be payable to the Sr. Accounts Officer, Directorate of IP&T, Port Blair. | Star CategoryFor Classification / ReclassificationSilver₹1,000/-Gold₹2,000/-
eligibility: A person holding property in A & N and willing to use a part of it to provide accommodation for Guests (Tourists) can Register the same under the Bed and Breakfast (B & B) Scheme of A & N Admin.; The property can be either “Owned” or “Rented / leased”. faqs.question: What is the objective of the Andaman & Nicobar Homestay Scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to provide clean, affordable, and quality accommodation for domestic and foreign tourists by allowing them to stay with Indian families and experience authentic Indian culture and cuisine.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Only homeowners who physically reside in the same premises with their family and are offering 1 to 6 rooms (max 12 beds) for guests are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What is the maximum number of rooms allowed under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Applicants can let out a minimum of one room and a maximum of six rooms, with a total capacity of up to 12 beds.

faqs.question: What are the star categories under the scheme?
faqs.answer: There are two classification categories: | - Silver | - Gold

faqs.question: What are the application fees for classification/reclassification?
faqs.answer: - Silver Category: ₹3,000- Gold Category: ₹5,000 | (As per latest fee structure for Andaman & Nicobar administration)

faqs.question: How long is the classification valid?
faqs.answer: The classification is valid for 3 years from the date of issue (or from the expiry date of the last classification if reapplying within 3 months before expiry).

faqs.question: What kind of food service is mandatory under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Only bed and breakfast is included. The type of breakfast offered must be clearly specified, priced, and communicated to the guests in advance.

faqs.question: Is there an inspection involved?
faqs.answer: Yes. Once an application is submitted, the establishment must be ready at all times for an onsite inspection by the Classification Committee. No postponement requests are allowed.

faqs.question: What is the application process for getting the Homestay license?
faqs.answer: Applicants must: | - Apply online or in-person at the Ministry of Tourism regional office.- Submit the completed application form with all required documents.- Pay the required fee.- Undergo site inspection. | - Receive approval/license within approximately 30 days, depending on completeness and location.

faqs.question: Where can one find the application form?
faqs.answer: The form can be obtained from the Ministry of Tourism's regional office or downloaded online (refer to page 9 of the official guidelines). If no regional office is available in the applicant’s area, the nearest state tourism office should be approached.

department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department

brief_description: The scheme "Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category)" provides 150 kg of BIS Type II concentrate feed to General Category livestock owners after parturition to support cattle health, increase milk production, and enhance calf development.
detailed_description: The scheme "Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category)" introduced by the Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Gujarat, is designed to support livestock owners during the critical post-parturition period, one month after delivery. This time is crucial for the health of the mother cattle and the calf. Under the scheme, 150 kg of BIS Type II concentrate feed is provided free of cost to livestock owners belonging to the General Category.

eligibility: The applicant must be a livestock owner.; The applicant must belong to the General Category.; The animal must have recently calved (given birth).
application_process: Step 1: The applicant may visit and apply online at I-Khedut Portal: https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/ | Step 2: On the home page, click on ‘Schemes’ and then click on ‘Animal Husbandry Schemes’. | Step 3: Now select the scheme, click on the ‘Apply’ button and an application page will open. | Step 4: Click on "Apply New" button and submit a new application. | Step 5: Click on the "Update Application" button to add corrections to the application. | Step 6: Once the application is done, confirm it. | Step 7: Take a print out of the confirmed application. | Step 8: Applicant can also check their Application Status/View/Print/Upload Application details from the below link: https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/public/frm_Applicant_Corner.aspx | Contact Us: Click here. | Note: Required Documents can also be submitted in hard copies to the office mentioned in the application form within 7 days.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the "Assistance of Concentrate Feed After Parturition (General Category)" scheme?
faqs.answer: The main objective of the scheme is to provide nutritional support to milch animals after parturition in the form of BIS Type II concentrate feed, helping to improve their health and milk production.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to benefit from this scheme?
faqs.answer: Livestock owners belonging to the General Category who meet the prescribed eligibility criteria are eligible to benefit from this scheme.

faqs.question: What kind of assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the scheme, eligible beneficiaries receive 150 kg of BIS Type II concentrate feed free of cost.

faqs.question: How often can a beneficiary avail the scheme?
faqs.answer: A beneficiary can avail the benefit of the scheme once every year.

faqs.question: Is there any cost to be paid by the applicant for the feed?
faqs.answer: No, the concentrate feed is provided with 100% assistance, meaning it is completely free for the eligible beneficiaries.

faqs.question: Can an applicant submit documents offline?
faqs.answer: Yes, the applicant can submit the required documents in hard copy to the concerned office within 7 days of applying online.

faqs.question: Can livestock owners from any category apply under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, this scheme is specifically designed for livestock owners belonging to the General Category.

faqs.question: What is the role of the calving certificate in the application process?
faqs.answer: The calving certificate confirms that the animal has recently given birth, which is essential for verifying the applicant’s eligibility.

faqs.question: What is BIS Type II concentrate feed?
faqs.answer: BIS Type II concentrate feed is a balanced and nutritious feed approved by the Bureau of Indian Standards, used to improve the health and milk yield of cattle.

faqs.question: Is it necessary for the animal to have recently calved to apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, only livestock owners whose animals have recently calved are eligible to apply under this scheme.

faqs.question: Where should an applicant apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant should apply online through the official iKhedut portal.

scheme_name: Award of Cash Incentive to the Toppers at Regional Level and Students Scoring Centum in the Subjects Involving Theory in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examinations in Government Schools in the Union Territory of Puducherry
tags: Student; Cash; Award; School; Education
brief_description: The scheme aims to award cash incentives to encourage students in their education by recognizing top three regional rank holders and those scoring centum in theory subjects in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Exams in Govt. Schools.
detailed_description: The scheme "Award of Cash Incentive to the Toppers at Regional Level and Students Scoring Centum in the Subjects Involving Theory in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examinations in Government Schools in the Union Territory of Puducherry" was launched by the Department of School Education, Puducherry. The quantum of Award ranges from ₹10,000/- up to ₹20,000/- for top ranks depending on the position, and ₹5,000/- per subject for centum scores.
benefits: - For students securing top three ranks at the regional level in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examinations in Government Schools: 1st Rank: ₹20,000/-; 2nd Rank: ₹15,000/-; 3rd Rank: ₹10,000/-. | - For students scoring centum in the subjects involving theory in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Higher Secondary Course Examinations: ₹5,000/- per subject. | - Mode of Disbursement: The award will be given through Direct Benefit Transfer or by Demand Draft.- Frequency: The award is disbursed to the eligible beneficiaries every year.- Tie-Breaker Condition: In the event of more than one student getting equal marks, the concerned full prize amount will be distributed to each of them in full. This distribution includes the marks secured by way of revaluation at a later date as prescribed by the concerned Board.
eligibility: The applicant must be a citizen of India.; The applicant must be a resident of the Union territory of Puducherry, by virtue of birth or continuous residence of not less than five years.; The applicant must be a student appearing in Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examinations in Government Schools.; The applicant must have passed the qualifying examination in the first attempt.; The applicant's marks from consecutive attempts must not be taken into account.
application_process: *The process is primarily an internal selection methodology conducted by the administering department based on examination results. | Step 1: Preparation of the List of Eligible Students | - The Directorate of School Education, Puducherry, will prepare the initial list of eligible students for the Award of cash incentive based on the total marks obtained in the respective Public Examination. | - This preparation utilizes the result analysis published by the concerned Board (Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examinations). | Step 2:*** Final Determination in Case of Disputes | - If any doubts or disputes arise concerning the selection or eligibility during the implementation of the Scheme, the matter shall be referred to the Secretary to Government (Education). | - The decision made by the Secretary to Government (Education) regarding the interpretation or clarification of any provision shall be considered final. | Disbursement of the Award*** | - Once the list of eligible beneficiaries is finalized annually, the corresponding cash award will be disbursed through either Direct Benefit Transfer or by Demand Draft. | - If multiple students secure equal marks, the full prize amount corresponding to the rank achieved will be distributed in full to each student, even if the marks were secured via revaluation.
documents_required: Proof Of Citizenship Of India.; Proof Of Residence In The Union Territory Of Puducherry.; Secondary School Leaving Certificate/Secondary School Certificate/Intermediate/Higher Secondary Public Examination Mark Sheet.; Proof Of Enrollment In A Government School.

faqs.question: If I achieve a centum score in a qualifying theory subject, how much money will I receive for each individual subject award?
faqs.answer: The cash award provided for scoring a centum in subjects involving theory in Secondary School Leaving Certificate or Higher Secondary Course Examinations is ₹5,000/- per subject.

faqs.question: What is the specific quantum of the cash incentive that a student is eligible to receive for achieving the Second Rank at the regional level?
faqs.answer: The award amount instituted for students who secure the Second Rank at the regional level in the respective Public Examination is ₹15,000/-.

faqs.question: To be considered eligible for this financial recognition program, is it a mandatory requirement that the applying student possesses Indian citizenship?
faqs.answer: Yes, the student must be a citizen of India to fulfill the basic requirements for receiving the award.

faqs.question: What is the established procedure if two or more students happen to obtain the exact same total marks, resulting in a tie for a ranked position?
faqs.answer: In the event of a tie, the concerned full prize amount corresponding to that rank will be distributed equally and in full to each of the students who share the equal marks.

faqs.question: If I achieve the First Rank at the regional level in my Public Examination, what is the exact amount of the cash award I will receive?
faqs.answer: Students securing the First Rank at the regional level in either the Secondary School Leaving Certificate or Higher Secondary level receive ₹20,000/-.

faqs.question: Besides being a citizen of India, what specific requirements regarding my residence must I meet within the Union territory of Puducherry?
faqs.answer: The student must be a resident of the Union territory of Puducherry, either by virtue of birth or through continuous residence for a minimum period of five years.

faqs.question: Which specific administrative regions within the Union territory of Puducherry are covered under the scope of this regional ranking scheme?
faqs.answer: The awards for regional toppers are applicable across the four regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, and Yanam.

faqs.question: Is there a specific condition related to the number of attempts I must take to pass the qualifying examination to be eligible for the financial award?
faqs.answer: Yes, the student must have successfully passed the qualifying examination on their first attempt to meet the eligibility requirements.

faqs.question: Could you please clarify which specific Public Examinations qualify a student for receiving a cash incentive under these guidelines?
faqs.answer: The examinations covered are the Secondary School Leaving Certificate, Secondary School Certificate, Intermediate, and Higher Secondary Public Examinations.

faqs.question: Are students attending any type of recognized educational institution allowed to apply for these merit-based cash incentives?
faqs.answer: No, the award is applicable only to students (both boys and girls) appearing in the Public Examinations from Government Schools.

faqs.question: Do the cash incentives offered for achieving a perfect score apply to all subjects, including both theory and practical components of the curriculum?
faqs.answer: The cash incentive for a perfect score is awarded specifically to students scoring centum only in subjects that involve a theory component.

faqs.question: If I secure the Third Rank among all eligible Government School students within my specific region, what financial incentive will be provided?
faqs.answer: Students who achieve the Third Rank at the regional level in either the Secondary School Leaving Certificate or Higher Secondary level are awarded ₹10,000/-.

faqs.question: If I attempt the qualifying examination more than once, will the scores from those subsequent or consecutive examinations be considered for ranking?
faqs.answer: No, marks obtained from any subsequent or consecutive attempts after the initial sitting shall not be taken into account for determining eligibility or ranking.

faqs.question: If my final marks increase after requesting a revaluation from the concerned Board, will these new, higher marks be considered for the cash award?
faqs.answer: Yes, marks secured by way of revaluation at a later date, as prescribed by the concerned Board, are included for considering the awards and resolving ties.

faqs.question: What is Silicosis?
faqs.answer: Silicosis is an incurable lung disease prevalent in workplaces like stone crushers and mines, caused by inhaling silica dust.

faqs.question: What are the symptoms of Silicosis?
faqs.answer: Symptoms include shortness of breath, fatigue, loss of appetite, chest pain, dry cough, respiratory failure, and it eventually leads to death.

faqs.question: What kind of financial assistance is provided under the scheme?
faqs.answer: A financial assistance of [?]1,00,000/- is provided.

faqs.question: Who receives the financial assistance if the deceased Silicosis victim was married?
faqs.answer: The widow or widower of the deceased receives the financial assistance.

faqs.question: Who receives the financial assistance if the deceased Silicosis victim was unmarried?
faqs.answer: The nominee of the deceased receives the financial assistance.

faqs.question: Where can affected Silicosis workers receive treatment?
faqs.answer: Workers under the Employee State Insurance Act, 1948 receive care at ESI hospitals, while others are treated at district hospitals and medical colleges by the Health Department.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility criteria for the scheme?
faqs.answer: The applicant must be the widow, widower, or nominee of a deceased worker who was confirmed to have Silicosis and was employed in a factory or at a construction site.

faqs.question: How can eligible applicants apply for the scheme benefits?
faqs.answer: Eligible applicants may visit the nearest Antyodaya Kendra and fill up the application form.

faqs.question: What are the benefits provided under the Scheme?
faqs.answer: Families of workers (Shramyogis) will receive financial assistance of [?]2,00,000/- in the event of the worker's death due to an accident during their course of employment.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the benefits under the scheme?
faqs.answer: The family of the worker is eligible for assistance under the scheme in the event of the worker's death due to an accident. Additionally, only workers (Shramyogis) whose factory/company/organization has regularly paid their Labour Welfare Fund are eligible.

faqs.answer: Yes, post-sickness and natural death of workers will not be admissible under the scheme.

brief_description: The Assam Government proposes to introduce a new module of “Aamar Dukan” namely “AAMAR DUKAN ON WHEELS” in the same line as the existing ‘Aamar Dukan’ on 22.02.2017.
detailed_description: Details | The Government proposes to introduce a new module of “Aamar Dukan” namely “AAMAR DUKAN ON WHEELS” in the same line as the existing ‘Aamar Dukan’. Under the new module, 22 Non-PDS items (which may increase to 36) will be delivered to the doorstep of the consumer at below MRP with a minimum profit margin. Eco-friendly E-rickshaws will be used as the transportation mode under the Scheme. Through this scheme, Government plans to promote cashless transactions as the E-Rickshaws will have a GPS-enabled smart phone, and Bluetooth billing printer which will be connected to the smart phone. | Objective | The basic objective of the Scheme Aamar Dukan on Wheels is to control the price of essential commodities by avoiding the middleman. Through this scheme, the consumers will get their daily requirements of essential commodities at their doorstep at a reasonable price and shall also contribute to the removal of the unemployment problem.
benefits: Benefits | - The beneficiary will keep the commodities allotted by the Department in case of AAMAR DUKAN on wheels in addition to other commodities. | - The selected beneficiaries of AAMAR DUKAN on wheels is allowed to take a profit margin of Rs. 2.00 to Rs. 3.00 per Kg./Per litre from consumers. | - The selected beneficiaries must abide by the direction of the Director, FCS&CA, Deputy Commissioners/Sub-Divisional Officers/Principal Secretaries of all Autonomous Councils. Any lapse on their part will be viewed seriously and legal action may be initiated also they will have to return the financial aid in addition to interest to the authority. | - The beneficiary should operate his shop as per the schedule specified by the authority. Any lapses in this regard will amount to the cancellation of his licence. | - The area of operation will be specified by the local authority for each beneficiary. | - The AAMAR DUKAN holders on wheels must display the displaying board of prices while distributing commodities. | - The AAMAR DUKAN holders on wheels will lift commodities from the selected wholesalers/stockists as per the direction of the respective Deputy Commissioners/Sub-Divisional Officers/Principal Secretaries of all Autonomous Councils. | - The beneficiary should operate his shop as per the schedule specified by the authority. Any lapses in this regard will amount to the cancellation of his licence. | - The AAMAR DUKAN on wheels should maintain the stock book and distribution register for inspecting authority.
eligibility: The applicant should be educated unemployed youth.; The applicant should be a permanent resident of Assam.; He should attain the age of 18 years and above.; His name should be registered in the Employment Exchange.; The minimum educational qualification will be HSLC or equivalent.
exclusions: Exclusions | - The candidate should not be less than 18 years of age. | - Candidates without registered in the Employment Exchange are not eligible. | - The minimum educational qualification will not be below HSLC or equivalent.
application_process: Application Process | - Deputy Commissioners/Sub-Divisional Officers/Principal Secretaries of all Autonomous Councils will invite applications and selection will be made on merit which includes | - Educational Qualification. | - Past experience if any, and | - Financial condition

detailed_description: The "Ashadeepa Scheme" was introduced by the Government of Karnataka in the 2017-18 budget to encourage private sector industries and companies to provide employment opportunities to persons belonging to the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories, ensuring social justice. faqs.question: What is the Ashadeepa Scheme?
faqs.answer: The Ashadeepa Scheme is a government initiative launched in 2017–18 to encourage private sector employers in Karnataka to hire candidates belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories, by offering financial reimbursements.

faqs.question: Who implements the Ashadeepa Scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme is implemented by the Karnataka State Workers Welfare and Social Security (Ashadeepa Scheme) Society (R) under the Labour Department of Karnataka.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of the Scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to create employment opportunities for SC/ST candidates in the private sector and improve their socio-economic condition through job placements and skill training.

faqs.question: What kind of financial support is offered to employers?
faqs.answer: Employers receive reimbursements for: | - ESI & EPF contributions | - Stipends paid during apprenticeship | - Salaries of newly hired SC/ST candidates | - Salaries post-apprenticeship recruitment

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Scheme?
faqs.answer: To be eligible, the candidate must: | - Be a resident of Karnataka | - Belong to the SC or ST category | - Be employed in a private-sector company or industry

faqs.question: Are apprentices covered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. SC/ST candidates undergoing apprenticeship training under the Apprenticeship Act, 1961, are eligible for stipend reimbursement to the employer.

faqs.question: What is reimbursed to employers for apprenticeship training?
faqs.answer: Employers are reimbursed up to ₹5,000 per month per apprentice, subject to 2/3rd of the actual stipend paid during one-year normal or two-year comprehensive training.

faqs.question: What if a company hires the apprentice after training?
faqs.answer: If an SC/ST apprentice is hired permanently, the employer is reimbursed 50% of the salary, up to ₹7,000/month, for a period of two years.

faqs.question: Is salary reimbursement available for direct recruitment?
faqs.answer: Yes. For SC/ST candidates directly employed after June 12, 2024, the employer is eligible for salary reimbursement up to ₹6,000/month for two years.

faqs.question: What is the reimbursement limit for ESI and EPF contributions?
faqs.answer: Employers can claim reimbursement up to ₹3,000 per month per candidate for 2 years for contributions made towards ESI and EPF.

faqs.question: Is skill development training provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes. The scheme supports Skill Development Training for SC/ST candidates through the Department of Skill Development, Entrepreneurship and Livelihood, Karnataka.

faqs.question: Can candidates apply for the scheme individually?
faqs.answer: No. The application must be submitted by the employer, not the individual candidate.

faqs.question: How does an employer apply for the Scheme?
faqs.answer: Employers can apply online via the Karnataka State Unorganized Workers Social Security Board website by filling out the Ashadeepa Scheme form and uploading required documents. https://kbocwwb.karnataka.gov.in/ashadeepaschemeform

scheme_name: Accidental Benefit
tags: Labour; Building Worker; Construction Worker; Accidental Benefit; Hospitalization; Disability
brief_description: The "Accidental Benefit'' scheme by the BOCW Welfare Board, Labour Department,West Bengal, is a welfare scheme that provides financial assistance to the beneficiary in case of hospitalization and disability due to an accident.
detailed_description: The "Accidental Benefit'' scheme by the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, West Bengal, is a welfare scheme for the registered workers of the board. Under this scheme, the Board shall provide financial assistance to a beneficiary in case of hospitalization for 5 or more days and become disabled due to an accident. A registered construction worker, who becomes permanently disabled, will be entitled to a monthly pension. Also in case of death of such pension holder, his/her spouse/nominee will be entitled to a monthly family pension.
benefits: - Hospitalization for 5 or more days: Up to a maximum amount of ₹10,000/-. - Disablement due to accident: Up to a maximum amount of ₹50,00/-. - Pension for permanent disablement: ₹750/- Per Month. - Family Pension for permanent disablement: ₹375/- Per Month (in case of death of such pension holder, his/her spouse/ nominee will be entitled to family pension).
eligibility: The applicant should be a resident of West Bengal.; The applicant should be a Building/ Construction Worker.; The applicant should be between 18 and 60 years.; The applicant should have engaged in building and construction work for at least 90 days in a given year.; The applicant should be a registered member Under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of West Bengal.; The member should have been hospitalized for 5 or more days or became disabled/permanently disabled due to an accident.

faqs.question: What is the age requirement for registration as a beneficiary under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of West Bengal?
faqs.answer: The building worker must be at least 18 years old and not older than 60 years old.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum service requirement to register as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: Yes, the building worker must have completed 90 days of service as a building worker in the preceding 12 months.

faqs.question: Who can apply for the welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: Any registered worker of the Board can apply for the welfare scheme.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for registering a worker as a beneficiary?
faqs.answer: At present all Assistant Labour Commissioners and Inspectors posted at blocks and municipalities shall be responsible for registering a worker as a beneficiary.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for registration as a beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Every building worker who is between the age of 18-60 years and who has been engaged in any building or other construction work for not less than 90 days during the preceding one year is eligible for registration as a beneficiary of the BOCW Welfare Board of West Bengal.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for applying for the registration?
faqs.answer: To register as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board, an applicant worker should collect and submit the Form-27 with all the mandatory documents (self attested, if required) and a fee of [?]20/- to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers.

faqs.question: Is there a specific form for the registration as a beneficiary under the BOCW Welfare Board?
faqs.answer: Yes, the application for registration must be made in Form-27. You can obtain this form from the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers in your area.

faqs.question: What happens after a construction worker is successfully verified for registration?
faqs.answer: Upon successful verification, the construction worker is registered, and an identity card and passbook are issued to him/her.

faqs.question: What are the fees associated with the registration process?
faqs.answer: The registration fee is [?]20/-, and the yearly subscription fee is [?]30/-. These amounts are noted in the passbook, and a receipt is issued.

faqs.question: How is the yearly subscription fee documented?
faqs.answer: The yearly subscription fee of [?]30/- is recorded in the passbook, and a receipt is issued for the payment.

faqs.question: What is the process for renewing the subscription after one year?
faqs.answer: After the expiry of one year, the subscription of the beneficiary is renewed upon payment of a renewal fee of [?]30/- and submission of an application made in Form-27A.

faqs.question: What happens if the subscription is not renewed after one year?
faqs.answer: If the subscription is not renewed, the registration of the beneficiary is cancelled after the expiry of one year.

faqs.question: Can a beneficiary reapply for renewal after cancellation?
faqs.answer: Yes, a fresh application for renewal can be submitted to the Assistant Labour Commissioner (ALC) for consideration.

faqs.question: What criteria must an applicant meet to be considered for this benefit?
faqs.answer: A registered member of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board of the West Bengal, who is been hospitalized for 5 or more days or has become disabled/permanently disabled due to an accident, shall be eligible for this benefit.

faqs.question: What is the maximum reimbursement amount for hospitalization for 5 or more days?
faqs.answer: The maximum reimbursement amount for hospitalization for 5 or more days is [?]10,000/-.

faqs.question: What are the benefits for disablement due to an accident?
faqs.answer: In the case of disablement due to an accident, the beneficiary can receive up to a maximum amount of [?]50,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly pension amount for permanent disablement?
faqs.answer: The monthly pension amount for permanent disablement is [?]750/-.

faqs.question: What is the family pension amount in case of the death of a pension holder with permanent disablement?
faqs.answer: In the case of the death of a pension holder with permanent disablement, the family pension amount for the spouse or nominee is [?]375/- per month.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the family pension for permanent disablement?
faqs.answer: The spouse or nominee of a pension holder with permanent disablement is eligible for the family pension.

faqs.question: What form needs to be used to apply for this welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: The application must be made in the prescribed Form-XXXIV. The form can be collected from Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers in your area.

faqs.question: Where do I submit the application for this welfare scheme?
faqs.answer: Submit your welfare scheme application to the Assistant Labour Commissioners/ Beneficiary Registering Officers in your area.

scheme_name: Agricultural Extension
ministry: Ministry Of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
department: Department of Agriculture Research and Education
tags: Agricultural; Extension
brief_description: Extension Division endeavours towards successful implementation of Agricultural Extension activities. Through its various programmes, schemes and activities, Extension Division helps farmers to get information regarding scientific research and new knowledge in agricultural practices.
detailed_description: Extension Division endeavours towards successful implementation of Agricultural Extension activities. Through its various programmes, schemes and activities, Extension Division helps farmers to get information regarding scientific research and new knowledge in agricultural practices. It assists and encourages the State Governments in organizing, maintaining and operating professional Extension Services. | Extension Division implements SMAE (Sub Mission on Agricultural Extension), a Sub Mission of KrishonnatiYojana. The popular ATMA Scheme which supports the State Governments in their extension activities is also run by Extension Division | The Division also provides Information Support to farmers in their agricultural activities. For this, it coordinates with Prasar Bharati and All India Radio in the effective running of the DD Kisan channel and Krishi Vani programmes respectively. Kisan Call Centres have been established at 21 locations across the country covering all states and UTs where the farmers can call on a toll free number (1800-180-1551) and get information regarding their area of interest in agriculture. Extension Division also publishes four magazines – two each in Hindi and English whereby information regarding various aspects of Extension activities and new developments is provided. | Schemes of Extension Division The Sub Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE) focuses on awareness creation and enhanced use of appropriate technologies in agriculture & allied sectors. It has four main components, namely: | - Support to State Extension Programmes for Extension Reforms | - Mass Media Support to Agricultural Extension | - Establishment of Agri-Clinic and Agri-Business Centres by Agriculture Graduates (ACABC). | - Extension Support to Central Institutions  |  The aforesaid components of Sub Mission on Agricultural Extension (SMAE) were run as separate schemes of the Extension Division. These were recently subsumed under the umbrella of SMAE.  |  Support to State Extension Programmes for Extension Reforms: As the name suggests, this scheme supports the state governments in their Extension Activities. It aims at making extension system farmers driven by way of new institutional arrangements for technology dissemination in the form of an Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA) at the district level to operationalise the extension reforms. Funds are released to State Governments in accordance with the scheme guideline which is also dependent on the State Governments releasing their share of contribution.  |  Mass Media Support to Agricultural Extension : | - Doordarshan and All India Radio | - Print Media | - Kisan Mela | - Kisan Call Centre | - Common Services Center.  |  Establishment of Agri-Clinic and Agri-Business Centres by Agriculture Graduates (ACABC) : This Programme aims to tap the expertise available in the large pool of Agriculture graduates, And a 45 days specialized training is provided by selected institutes across the country.  |  Extension Support to Central Institutions This scheme aims towards capacity building of Extension functionaries and also, towards skill development of rural youth, farmers and farm women. The prominent institutions involved in this effort are – the Directorate of Extension (a subordinate office under the Extension Division), MANAGE, Hyderabad (an autonomous institute associated with Extension Division), four Extension Education Institutes (EEIs) at the Regional level and the State Agricultural Management & Extension Training Institutes (SAMETIs) at the State level.  |  The main programmes under the scheme are as under: | A. Programmes for Capacity Building: | - Extension Education Institutes (EEIs): - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare has established four Extension Education Institutes at Nilokheri (Haryana); Hyderabad (Telangana); Anand (Gujarat) and Jorhat (Assam). These EEIs cater to the training needs of middle-level field extension functionaries working under agriculture and allied departments of States/UTs of respective regions. The programmatic activities of EEIs include the organization of on-campus/off-campus training, workshops, conferences etc. in the areas of communication technology, extension methodology, training management, Agriculture Knowledge Information System (AKIS) and Information Technology. | - Model Training Courses(MTCs): - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare has established four Extension Education Institutes at Nilokheri (Haryana); Hyderabad (Telangana); Anand (Gujarat) and Jorhat (Assam). These EEIs cater to the training needs of middle-level field extension functionaries working under agriculture and allied departments of States/UTs of respective regions. The programmatic activities of EEIs include the organization of on-campus/off-campus training, workshops, conferences etc. in the areas of communication technology, extension methodology, training management, Agriculture Knowledge Information System (AKIS) and Information Technology.  |  B. Kisan Call Center(KCC) | - The project aims to answer farmers’ queries on a telephone call in their own dialect. Presently these call centres are working in 21 different locations covering all the States and UTs. A countrywide common eleven-digit Toll-Free Number 1800-180-1551 has been allotted for Kisan Call Center. This number is accessible through mobile phones and landlines of all telecom networks including private service providers. Replies to the farmers’ queries are available from 6:00 am to 10:00 pm on all seven days of the week. | - Kisan Call Center agents are known as Farm Tele Advisors (FTAs), who are graduates or above in agriculture or allied areas and possess excellent communication skills in their respective local languages. Queries which cannot be answered by FTAs are transferred to higher-level experts in call conferencing mode. These experts are subject matter specialists of State Agricultural Departments, ICAR & State Agricultural Universities. | - The restructured KCC has a number of unique features viz. 100% call recording; call barging; voice mail service; customized IVRs; call conferencing through the experts; playing state-specific advisories during call wait time; SMS to caller farmers giving a gist of answers given by FTAs and also, registration of farmers for receiving SMS from experts on the subject area provided by them for receiving regular updates on selected crops.  |  Programmes for Skill Development: | - Skill Training of Rural Youth(STRY): - The component aims at training rural youths, rural artisans (blacksmiths, carpenters etc. designing/manufacturing farm implements) including farm women across the country. The training under this component focuses on specific vocational areas in agriculture & allied sectors. Both Public and Private/Non-Governmental Institutions including Vocational Training organisations, Youth Organisations (like Nehru Yuva Kendra) are actively involved in the implementation of this programme. | - Diploma in Agricultural Extension Services for Input Dealers (DAESI): -Agri-Input Dealers in the country are a prime source of farm information to the farming community, besides the supply of inputs and credit. However, the majority of these dealers do not have formal agricultural education. In order to build their technical competency in agriculture and to facilitate them to serve the farmers better and to act as Para–Extension professionals, a self-financed “One-year Diploma in Agricultural Extension Services for Input Dealers (DAESI) Program” has been launched during the year 2003 with a course fee of Rs.20000/- to the input dealers. The National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE) is the nodal agency to run this program.
eligibility: Graduates in agriculture and allied subjects like Horticulture, Sericulture, Dairy, Animal Husbandry, Fisheries, Home/ Community Sciences, Biotechnology, Agricultural Engineering, Forestry, Food Technology, Food Nutrition, and Dietetics, etc, from SAUs/ Central Agricultural Universities/ Universities and graduates in Environmental Science, Botany, Zoology and Chemistry recognized by ICAR/ UGC. Degrees in Agriculture and allied subjects offered by other agencies are also considered subject to the approval of the Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Government of India on the recommendation of the State Government.; Diploma (with at least 50% marks)/ Post Graduate Diploma holders in Agriculture and allied subjects (as in para 3.1) from State Agricultural Universities, State Agriculture and Allied Departments and the State Department of Technical Education. Diplomas in Agriculture and allied subjects offered by other agencies (autonomous bodies, UGC affiliated universities, etc.) are also considered subject to the approval of the Department of Agriculture  & Cooperation, Government of India on the recommendation of the State Government.; Post Graduation in Agriculture & allied subjects.; Degree courses recognized by UGC have more than 60 percent of the course content in Agriculture and allied subjects 3.5.; Diploma/ Post-graduate Diploma courses with more than 60 percent of course content in Agriculture and allied subjects after B.Sc. in Biological Sciences from  recognized  colleges  and universities,; Agriculture-related courses at the intermediate (i.e. plus two)  level, with at least 55% marks,; The scheme covers full financial support for training and handholding, provision of loans, and credit-linked back-ended composite subsidy.

scheme_name: Art Exhibition Assistance in the State
department: Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department
tags: Art Exhibition; Financial Assistance; Group Exhibition; Lalitkala Academy
brief_description: The scheme "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" by the Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department, Government of Gujarat aims to promote visual arts by supporting local artists through financial assistance.
detailed_description: The scheme "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" by the Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department, Government of Gujarat aims to encourage visual artists of Gujarat to showcase their work by offering financial support for organizing exhibitions across the state. The scheme particularly targets those who have either undergone formal art education or have experience in holding art exhibitions. This initiative helps elevate the reach and recognition of regional art and artists. The scheme is implemented by the Gujarat State Lalitkala Academy.
benefits: - Financial Assistance: Up to ₹25,000/- or actual expenses incurred (whichever is less) for organizing an art exhibition.
eligibility: The applicant should be a resident of Gujarat.; The applicant should have received formal art education or should have conducted a previous individual or group art exhibition.; The applicant should organize an exhibition within Gujarat.; The applicant should exhibit a minimum of 30 artworks in the sponsored exhibition.
application_process: Step 1: The interested applicant should download the prescribed format of the application form. | Step 2: In the application form, provide all the mandatory details, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). | Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the supporting documents to the below address of the Gujarat State Lalitkala Academy. | Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgement from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. | Contact Us: | Gujarat State Lalit Kala Academy | Ravishankar Raval Kala Bhavan, | In front of the Bhaikaka building, | Law Garden, Ellisbridge, | Ahmedabad - 380006, | Phone: 079-26425562; 079-26562558
documents_required: Proof of age (must be over 18 years).; Proof of Gujarat residency.; Art-related qualification certificate (e.g., Diploma in Fine Arts or Art Teacher Diploma).; Photographs of the artwork (up to 3 entries).; Details of exhibitions/awards if applicable.; Self-declaration confirming originality.; Bank details (if applying for financial support).

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for financial assistance under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme?
faqs.answer: An applicant is eligible for financial assistance under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme if they are an original resident of Gujarat, have received a formal art education or have previously organized an individual or group art exhibition, and if they plan to exhibit a minimum of 30 artworks within the state of Gujarat.

faqs.question: What kind of exhibitions are supported under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme supports physical art exhibitions that are organized within the boundaries of Gujarat, provided the artist exhibits at least 30 original works of art, regardless of whether the exhibition is individual or group-based.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory for the artist to have a formal education in art to avail of the benefits of this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, it is not mandatory for the applicant to have formal education in art as the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme also considers applicants who have previously held individual or group art exhibitions.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance can an eligible artist receive under this scheme?
faqs.answer: An eligible artist can receive financial assistance of up to ₹25,000/- or the total actual expenditure incurred for organizing the exhibition, whichever amount is lower, under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme.

faqs.question: Can an exhibition organized outside Gujarat be considered under this scheme?
faqs.answer: No, exhibitions that are held outside the state of Gujarat are not eligible for financial assistance under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme, as it is exclusively intended to promote art within the state.

faqs.question: Is there any specific number of artworks required to be exhibited for eligibility under the scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, in order to be considered eligible for financial assistance under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme, the artist must exhibit a minimum of 30 artworks in the sponsored exhibition.

faqs.question: What kind of documentation is required to apply for the scheme?
faqs.answer: To apply for the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme, the applicant must submit proof of residence in Gujarat, proof of formal art education or evidence of previous exhibitions, identity proof, original bills or vouchers of expenses incurred, and a list of 30 exhibited artworks.

faqs.question: When is the financial assistance disbursed to the eligible applicant?
faqs.answer: Financial assistance under the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme is disbursed only after the successful completion of the exhibition and verification of the original vouchers or bills submitted by the applicant.

faqs.question: Does the scheme cover the expenses of digital or online exhibitions?
faqs.answer: No, the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme only supports physical exhibitions held within the state, and it does not include support for online or digital exhibitions.

faqs.question: Are there any income limits or restrictions based on financial status for this scheme?
faqs.answer: There are no income limits or financial status restrictions for applying to the "Art Exhibition Assistance in the State" scheme, making it accessible to all eligible artists regardless of their economic background.

brief_description: The scheme aims to promote fine arts by providing financial assistance of up to ₹1,00,000 to artists from Gujarat for organizing art exhibitions abroad and in other states of India.
detailed_description: The scheme "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" by the Sports, Youth and Cultural Activities Department, Government of Gujarat aims to encourage and promote artists originally from Gujarat in the field of fine arts—such as painting, sculpture, graphic arts, and photography—by offering financial assistance to organize exhibitions abroad and outside the state. The scheme ensures support for artists with a record of conducting prior solo or group exhibitions, helping them to gain national and international exposure through structured financial aid. The scheme is implemented by the Gujarat State Fine Arts Academy.

faqs.question: What is the objective of the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme?
faqs.answer: The primary objective of the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme is to promote and support artists from Gujarat by providing them with financial assistance to organize their exhibitions outside the state and internationally, thereby helping them gain broader exposure and recognition in the field of fine arts.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme?
faqs.answer: Any artist who is originally from Gujarat and has previously organized either 3 to 5 solo exhibitions or 5 to 8 group exhibitions in the field of fine arts such as painting, sculpture, graphic arts, or photography is eligible to apply for the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme.

faqs.question: What type of assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Under the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme, eligible artists are provided financial support up to ₹1,00,000/- along with reimbursement for airfare and visa expenses specifically for organizing exhibitions in foreign countries.

faqs.question: How many times can an artist receive benefits under this scheme?
faqs.answer: An artist is allowed to avail the financial benefit under the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme only once for organizing an exhibition abroad and up to three times during their career for organizing exhibitions outside the state of Gujarat.

faqs.question: Is there a specific number of artworks that need to be displayed in the exhibition?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme, it is mandatory for the artist to display at least 30 original artworks during the exhibition supported through this assistance.

faqs.question: Are there any venue-related requirements for organizing the exhibitions under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, as per the conditions of the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme, the artist is required to organize two exhibitions, including a preview exhibition at the Ravi Shankar Rawal Kala Bhavan and the main exhibition at the applied-for location either abroad or outside the state.

faqs.question: What is the procedure for submitting an application under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The artist must submit their application in the prescribed format within the designated application window announced between April 1 and May 15 each year through public advertisements in daily newspapers as part of the process for the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for the implementation of this scheme?
faqs.answer: The implementation of the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme is carried out by the Gujarat State Fine Arts Academy, which manages the selection, scrutiny, and approval of applications submitted by eligible artists.

faqs.question: How are the applications evaluated and selected for assistance?
faqs.answer: All applications received under the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme are evaluated by an Artist Selection Committee, which scrutinizes the applications and grants approval based on the eligibility and merit of the artist’s prior work and proposed exhibition.

faqs.question: Is the assistance amount provided in advance or after the exhibition is conducted?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance under the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme is disbursed only after the successful conduct of the exhibition and the submission of a detailed expenditure report audited by a chartered accountant.

faqs.question: Are group exhibitions eligible under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, the "Assistance for Exhibitions Abroad and Out of State" scheme allows applications for both individual and group exhibitions, provided that the artists involved meet the eligibility criteria and the exhibition satisfies the stipulated conditions.

faqs.question: What is required for all claims to be supported according to the provided content?
faqs.answer: All claims must be supported by a certificate issued by a Chartered Accountant.

faqs.question: How much employment must be provided to residents of Puducherry for a unit to be eligible for incentives/subsidies/assistance?
faqs.answer: At least 60% of employment must be provided to the people of Puducherry out of the total employment strength of the industrial units.

faqs.question: What is the composition of the State Level Committee responsible for evaluating subsidy applications?
faqs.answer: The State Level Committee consists of the Secretary to Government (Industries & Commerce), the Managing Director of PIPDIC, the Deputy Secretary/Under Secretary (Finance), and the Director of Industries and Commerce, all from Puducherry.

faqs.question: Under what circumstances would the entire amount of subsidies and incentives availed need to be refunded, according to the content?
faqs.answer: If the unit undergoes any amendments in new partners or shareholders within five years from the date of availing the subsidy, the entire amount of subsidies and incentives availed must be refunded with a simple interest of 14% per annum.

faqs.question: Which types of investments are ineligible for investment subsidy according to the provided conditions?
faqs.answer: Working capital, commissioning fees, goodwill fees, royalty, preliminary and pre-operative expenses, capitalized interest, transportation and erection charges, goods vehicles, office equipment, furniture, crates, pallets, and consumable stores, etc., are ineligible for investment subsidy.

faqs.question: Through whom is the subsidy amount disbursed if the unit is financed by financial institutions/banks?
faqs.answer: The subsidy amount is disbursed through financial institutions/banks towards the adjustment against the loan availed by the entrepreneurs or for the creation of additional fixed assets or for working capital purposes.

faqs.question: How is the subsidy disbursed for self-financed units?
faqs.answer: For self-financed units, the subsidy is disbursed directly to the entrepreneur/unit.

faqs.question: What happens if an industrial unit has availed investment subsidy from the Central Government/State Government or any other agency?
faqs.answer: If an industrial unit has availed investment subsidy from any other agency, it is not eligible to apply for a subsidy for the same investment again under this Scheme.

faqs.question: What is the condition for industrial units set up by the same person to be eligible for subsidy as separate entities?
faqs.answer: Industrial units set up by the same person as proprietor, common partners, or common Board of Directors/shareholders are eligible for subsidy as separate entities provided the location of the units is different and licenses/clearances/registrations are obtained separately for the enterprises.

faqs.question: How is the commencement date for regular commercial production determined?
faqs.answer: The commencement date is verified by Officials of the Industries Department based on the entrepreneur's admission.

faqs.question: What is the employment requirement for qualifying for incentives/subsidies?
faqs.answer: To qualify for incentives/subsidies, the industrial unit must provide at least 60% of employment to residents of Puducherry out of the total employment strength.

faqs.question: What is the role of the State Level Committee in the subsidy application process?
faqs.answer: The State Level Committee scrutinizes applications, determines eligibility, and recommends the quantum of incentive/subsidy admissible to the unit.

eligibility: The applicant should be a native of Rajasthan.; The applicant should be the widow of an ex-serviceman of the rank of Havildar or below.; The assistance is available for a maximum of two daughters of the widow of an ex-serviceman.; The daughter should be at least 18 years of age at the time of marriage.; The daughter’s name should be duly recorded in the ex-serviceman’s discharge book or Part-2 order.; The applicant should possess a valid Ex-Serviceman/Widow Identity Card issued by the respective District Sainik Welfare Office.; The applicant should not have received marriage assistance for the same purpose from the Kendriya Sainik Board.; The application should be submitted within one year from the date of marriage to be eligible for assistance under this scheme.; Widows of ex-servicemen who are classified as Battle Casualties or Physical Casualties (attributable cases) are not eligible under this scheme, as marriage assistance in such cases is provided by the Army Headquarters.; If the applicant is eligible for the Daughter Marriage Assistance Scheme run by the Kendriya Sainik Board for ex-servicemen, then financial aid from the Amalgamated Fund shall not be granted.; The benefit shall be extended only to the widow of an ex-serviceman who meets the definition of an ex-serviceman as prescribed by the Government of India.
application_process: Application Process: | Step 1: The interested applicant should visit the office of the District Sainik Welfare Officer and request a hard copy of the prescribed format of the application form from the staff exclusively entrusted to issue and collect filled-in applications. | OR | The applicant should download the application form (Page No. 4) from the official website. | Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest if required). | Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the District Sainik Welfare Officer. | Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the District Sainik Welfare Officer to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission and a unique identification number (if applicable). | NOTE: | - The application must be submitted within one year of the marriage date. | - The application should be made through the same District Sainik Welfare Officer from whom the ex-serviceman/widow's identity card was issued. | Post-Application Process: | Step 1: The District Sainik Welfare Officer will verify the application and documents. | Step 2: Verified applications will be forwarded to the Director, Sainik Kalyan Vibhag, Rajasthan. A committee will review applications every six months. | Step 3: If approved, the financial assistance will be transferred online to the applicant’s bank account. | Step 4: The District Sainik Welfare Officer will inform the applicant about the payment status.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Widows of ex-servicemen (Havildar or below rank) who have not availed marriage assistance from the Central Sainik Board.

faqs.question: What is the amount provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: ₹25,000/- per daughter, up to two daughters.

faqs.question: Can I apply if my husband was a battle casualty?
faqs.answer: No, as separate financial assistance is provided by the Army Headquarters.

faqs.question: Can I apply for more than two daughters?
faqs.answer: No, assistance is provided for a maximum of two daughters.

faqs.question: Is there any income limit for eligibility?

faqs.question: What is the application deadline?

faqs.question: How is the assistance amount disbursed?
faqs.answer: Through an online transfer to the applicant’s bank account.

faqs.question: How can I apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: Submit the prescribed application form with required documents to the District Sainik Welfare Officer.

faqs.question: What if I have already received assistance from the Central Sainik Board?
faqs.answer: The applicant will not be eligible for this scheme.

faqs.question: Can an applicant from another state apply?

benefits: - An amount of ₹51,000/- for each marriage is provided. | Note: Assistance is provided for the marriage of up to two daughters of the registered worker as well as for the worker’s own marriage.

brief_description: A scheme to provide financial assistance to a non-pensioner Ex-Servicemen of all ranks and widows to meet medical expenses related to treatment of approved serious diseases like cancer, renal failure, knee replacement and heart surgery.
detailed_description: A scheme to provide financial assistance to a non-pensioner Ex-Servicemen of all ranks and widows to meet medical expenses related to treatment of approved serious diseases like cancer, renal failure, knee replacement and heart surgery.  |  Expenditure must be incurred at a approved govt hospital at the rates applicable under CGHS / ECHS.  |  List of the serious diseases are covered under this scheme | - Angiography & Angioplasty | - CABG. faqs.question: Can I Take The Benefit Of This Scheme For Treatment In Any Private Or Government Hospital?

faqs.question: Can I Give Bank Details Of Any Bank?

scheme_name: Financial Assistance For Procuring Mobility Equipment To Disabled Ex-Servicemen (All Ranks)
tags: Ex-Servicemen; Person With Disability; Sainik; Handicapped; ESM
brief_description: The scheme provides financial assistance of a maximum of ₹ 1,00,000 from the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF) for the procurement of modified scooters, crutches and wheelchairs for Ex-Servicemen who are disabled after their retirement from service with a disability of 50% or more.
detailed_description: The scheme "Financial Assistance For Procuring Mobility Equipment To Disabled Ex-Servicemen(All Ranks)" by the Department of Ex-Servicemen Welfare of the Ministry of Defence, provide financial assistance for the procurement of modified scooter for those Ex-Servicemen (ESM), who are disabled after their retirement from service with disability of 50% or more. After their retirement, most of the ESMs continue to be engaged in physically challenging activities/work. Some of them unfortunately become handicapped due to accidents etc after their retirement and need mobility equipment such as modified scooters, crutches and wheelchairs to carry on with their life. To procure mobility requirements, the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) provides financial assistance to disabled ESMs from the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund (AFFDF).
benefits: - A financial assistance of a maximum of ₹ 1,00,000.1. The beneficiary can re-apply for new mobility equipment after the lapse of 10 years from the date of purchase of the previous equipment.
eligibility: The applicant should be an Ex-Serviceman.; The applicant should be disabled after retirement from the service.; The percentage of the disability should be 50% or more.; The applicant should not be covered under a similar scheme of the Army/Navy/Air Force.; The application of the applicant should be recommended by the respective Zila Sainik Board (ZSB).; The applicant should be capable of personally utilizing the mobility equipment provided.
application_process: Step 1: In the Registration Form, fill in all the mandatory fields and upload the required documents. | Step 2: Fill in the verification code, and click "Submit" to complete your registration. | Step 3: Take a print of the submitted registration form, attach the self-attested copies of the required documents, and submit the same at the respective ZSB. | Post-Application Processes | Step 1: The Zila Sainik Welfare Office (ZSWO) will scrutinize the application, and if found correct in all respects, will forward it directly to Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) Secretariat for payment. | Step 2: On receipt at the KSB Secretariat, the Welfare Section-in-Charge will assign the application to a particular clerk who will enter desired data from the applications into the computer. Another clerk will be designated to check the correctness of the entries. | Step 3: The Section-in-Charge will verify the same and put up the case in the relevant file for processing to JD(Welfare) who will obtain the approval of the Secretary, KSB. | Step 4: After approval at KSB, the application will be processed for payment. | Track Application Status | Step 1: Visit the Official Website of the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) and click the “Status of Application”. | Step 2: Enter your DAK ID and the verification code. Click on the “Search” button to check the status of your application.
documents_required: Complete Discharge Book/Document/Certificate.; ESM Identity Card.; Documentary evidence showing the nature of activity in which disabled.; Disability Certificate issued by Armed Forces Medical Authority, indicating nature of disability and recommended procurement of mobility equipment.; Financial estimate for a modified scooter from an authorized dealer indicating type, make and specifications of the mobility equipment.; Details of Bank A/c No (in PNB/SBI only) and IFS Code.

faqs.question: What is the process for reapplying for new mobility equipment after the initial 10-year period?
faqs.answer: After the expiration of the 10-year lifespan of the mobility equipment, beneficiaries are eligible to reapply for new equipment. They would need to follow the same application process and provide updated documentation, including a new financial estimate for the equipment. The application is then reviewed and processed as before.

faqs.question: Are there any restrictions on the type of mobility equipment that can be procured with the financial assistance provided by the scheme?
faqs.answer: The financial assistance can be used for any mobility equipment that aids the Ex-Serviceman's mobility needs. This can include wheelchairs, crutches, or other devices deemed necessary.

faqs.question: How can applicants track the status of their applications?
faqs.answer: Applicants can check the status of their applications by visiting the official website of the Kendriya Sainik Board and clicking on the "Status of Application" link. They need to enter their DAK ID and verification code to check the status.

faqs.question: How does the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) process the applications after receiving them?
faqs.answer: The KSB Secretariat assigns applications to clerks for data entry and verification. The Section-in-Charge and JD(Welfare) verify and process the applications, and upon approval, they are processed for payment.

faqs.question: What role does the Zila Sainik Welfare Office (ZSWO) play in the application process?
faqs.answer: The ZSWO plays a crucial role in scrutinizing the application. If the application is found correct in all respects, it is forwarded to the Kendriya Sainik Board (KSB) Secretariat for further processing.

faqs.question: What documents are required for the application?
faqs.answer: Applicants need to submit several documents, including their complete Discharge Book/Document/Certificate, ESM Identity Card, Disability Certificate issued by Armed Forces Medical Authority, and financial estimates for the modified scooter, among others.

faqs.question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides a maximum financial assistance of [?]1,00,000 to eligible disabled Ex-Servicemen.

faqs.question: What is the aim of the "Financial Assistance For Procuring Mobility Equipment To Disabled Ex-Servicemen" scheme?
faqs.answer: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to disabled Ex-Servicemen who have a disability of 50% or more after their retirement from service. This assistance is for the procurement of modified scooters and other mobility equipment to help them lead independent lives.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
faqs.answer: To be eligible, applicants must be Ex-Servicemen who have become disabled after their retirement from service, with a disability percentage of 50% or more. They should not be covered under a similar scheme by the Army, Navy, or Air Force.
